text:
maya: quick thought — can we land a tiny enforcement-shim at the gateway to handle quotas + routing for REST clients so we don't have to change every backend proto right away?

alex: like a compatibility layer that translates REST->gRPC + attaches proto headers?

maya: yeah. minimal behavior: map incoming REST route to canonical service name, validate API key, emit quota token, and forward as gRPC call to the same backend. no business logic change.

bjorn: main risks: streaming endpoints and binary payloads. also we lose some fine-grained telemetry unless we inject extra markers.

maya: agreed. proposal: shim only for unary endpoints initially. streaming remains direct gRPC clients. fallback 415 for unsupported content-type.

alex: how would quotas be enforced? shared quota service or local token bucket at the shim?

maya: prefer centralized quota service for consistency (same as dedicated mode). shim calls quota/ingest and attaches X-RD-Quota-Grant header. if denied, return 429 early.

taylor: we need route-level telemetry in observability — token breakdown by model/route. shim should emit structured spans with route, model_hint, and quota_decision. otherwise console dashboards will be blind.

bjorn: can we implement shim as an Envoy WASM filter? that gives us per-request hooks, stats, and integrates with existing traces. WASM also lets us keep it config-driven so we can flip mapping rules.

maya: thinking along same lines. config snippet suggestion: 
```yaml
- match: "/v1/generate"
  map_to: "inference.generate_unary"
  mode: unary
  quota_key: "api_key"
- match: "/v1/stream"
  mode: passthrough
```

alex: +1 for Envoy WASM. downside: team ramp for WASM dev, and we need thorough tests for header mapping.

bjorn: also watch out for auth semantics — don't re-sign JWTs in the shim. forward original auth to backends and only consult quota service with a token derived from api_key.

maya: good call. shim should never mutate identity header except to attach internal X-RD-Quota-Grant. backends still validate JWTs.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: enforcement-shim v0.1 -> eng-platform-ns (5% traffic) :rocket:

alex: quick checklist before we expand canary: 1) quota service rejects known bad keys 2) telemetry spans show route mapping 3) e2e test for unary payload pass-through 4) 429 behavior documented in console UX

ops-bot: adding a follow-up RFC item: "shim rollout plan + telemetry signals". please add specific dashboard panels (quota grant ratio, 429 rate by route, mapping failures).

maya: I'll draft the RFC and include example dashboards. can we get access to sample traffic for mapping tests?

bjorn: I'll generate a small replay from prod traces (redacted) and hand it to you.

alex: if this works, it buys us months to migrate services to proto-first without breaking customers. we should also surface the migration schedule in the console so teams know when the shim will be removed.

maya: yep — console feature: "compat_shim: mapped_routes" with planned deprecation date. short-term UX: show which clients are hitting shim vs native gRPC.

ops-bot: noted. created task PLAT-4823 for console panel.

maya: thanks all — will post RFC draft later today.
